provider: NOAA National Weather Service – National Hurricane Center (NHC) and Central Pacific Hurricane Center
description: Latest official status of every active tropical or subtropical cyclone in the Atlantic, Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific basins: position, classification, intensity, pressure, motion and links to the current advisories.

coverage.geographic: North Atlantic, Eastern North Pacific and Central North Pacific basins only (NHC and CPHC areas of responsibility).
coverage.temporal: Currently active cyclones only; the file is empty outside of active periods.

updateCadence.upstream: With every advisory (every 6 hours, intermediate advisories every 3 hours near land)

attribution: NOAA National Weather Service, National Hurricane Center

license.name: U.S. Government work – public domain (NWS data may be used for any lawful purpose without implying endorsement)
license.notes: NWS disclaimer: information on NWS web pages is in the public domain unless noted otherwise; it must not be presented as official government material after modification, and use must not imply endorsement by NOAA/NWS.

limitations: Only storms in the NHC/CPHC basins are listed; Western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Southern Hemisphere cyclones are not covered.
The file shows the latest advisory position only – no forecast track, cone or wind radii (those are linked as separate GIS files).
Published by NHC as an experimental product; the file may briefly lag the text advisories.
The start of the record is the time of the latest status update, not the time the cyclone formed.
confidenceNotes: Positions and intensities are official NHC advisory values; the file carries no numeric uncertainty, so no confidence value is given. Severity is derived by this application from the advisory intensity (maximum sustained wind): below 34 kt minor, 34–63 kt moderate, 64–95 kt severe, 96 kt and above (major hurricane) extreme; when intensity is missing the classification code is used instead.

retention.note: A storm is kept while NHC lists it as active and for 30 days after it disappears from the file.

layers.name: Active tropical cyclones (NHC)
layers.description: Official current position, classification and intensity of active tropical cyclones in the Atlantic and Eastern/Central Pacific from the U.S. National Hurricane Center.
